fixes.explanation: I see why you'd pick it, since commanding sounds like what leaders do. But that isn't the word Jesus uses. He says the kings of the Gentiles lord it over people, then tells the disciples, “But you shall not be like them.” The line is, “…and the one who leads like the one who serves.”
Table it is, baker. Jesus says, “…so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom…” I spent years in a junk drawer, so a seat at a table sounds like a promotion to me.

An altar sounds serious, and I see the pull. But Jesus pairs the eating and drinking with His table: “…so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom…” That's a meal, friend, and a meal means somebody pulled out a chair.

A gate is a way in, and I see the pull. But Jesus talks about eating and drinking: “…so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom…” In my bakery, nobody ever got handed a cookie at a gate. You get it at the table.

Yes, baker. Jesus says they will “…sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” He says it in the same talk where He answers their dispute over who's greatest. I think that's one humbling seat at the table.

That's right, baker. Jesus says to Simon, “But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail.” Simon is the disciple Jesus also named Peter (Luke 6:14). Satan, the devil, has asked to sift them like wheat, and Jesus has prayed for him. That's Jesus covering Simon.

An angel on guard is a nice picture, but the text doesn't say it. What Jesus says is, “But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail.” Simon is the disciple Jesus also named Peter (Luke 6:14). The thing Jesus names is His prayer.

Hiding is a natural guess when someone's about to be sifted, but Jesus doesn't tell Simon to hide. He says, “But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail.” Simon is the disciple Jesus also named Peter (Luke 6:14). And Jesus follows it by giving him a job.

That's what he says, baker. Peter, the disciple also called Simon (Luke 6:14), answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.” That's a big promise to make at a table. Next Jesus answers him.

A storm and a sea sound like a big adventure, so I see the mix-up. But here, Peter, the disciple also called Simon (Luke 6:14), says, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.” No water in this one, friend.

Desert and wild country are good guesses for a story like this, but Peter doesn't say them. Peter, the disciple also called Simon (Luke 6:14), says, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.” Prison and death are the two things he names. Friend, that's serious loyalty talk.

That's right, baker. Jesus says, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.” It's hard to hear right after Peter's big promise. I think that one stings.

Yes, baker. Jesus asks, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” and they answer, “Nothing.” Without a purse, bag or sandals, they still lacked nothing. That's a one-word answer you don't see every day.
Yes, baker. When the disciples say, “Look, Lord, here are two swords.” Jesus answers, “That is enough…” He doesn't send them off for more. The story still has more to tell.
